title: Map Analysis
modules: Below For A Discussion On Each Of The Methods For
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is one of the most important elements of a map."
Scale is one of the most important elements of a map.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the angle or inclination of any side of a highland (hill or mountain)."
Slope refers to the angle or inclination of any side of a highland (hill or mountain).
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a long, narrow depression in-between two highlands."
Valleys and Spurs A valley is a long, narrow depression in-between two highlands.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a measure of the level of compactness of a particular point feature distributed over a geographical space."
Density is a measure of the level of compactness of a particular point feature distributed over a geographical space.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to the arrangement or layout of buildings in a settlement."
Settlement pattern refers to the arrangement or layout of buildings in a settlement.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a map of the different types of rocks that are on the surface of the Earth."
Geologic Maps A geologic map is a map of the different types of rocks that are on the surface of the Earth.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an accurate representation of the spherical shape of the world."
A globe is an accurate representation of the spherical shape of the world.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a map that represents the physical features of an area such as: vegetation, mountains, rivers, sea and lakes."
Physical Map A physical map is a map that represents the physical features of an area such as: vegetation, mountains, rivers, sea and lakes.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the mathematical transformation of the spherical Earth unto a flat medium."
Map projection is the mathematical transformation of the spherical Earth unto a flat medium.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is used to compare the relationship between a stream order and the next higher stream order."
Bifurcation ratio (Br) is used to compare the relationship between a stream order and the next higher stream order.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are one of the world's oldest types of document and means of communication."
Maps are one of the world's oldest types of document and means of communication.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to both the study of maps and the process of map-making."
Cartography refers to both the study of maps and the process of map-making.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are used to geographically reference the positions of features on the surface of the Earth."
The coordinates are used to geographically reference the positions of features on the surface of the Earth.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are used to draw a map; each symbol represents a particular category of geographical feature."
Graphic symbols are used to draw a map; each symbol represents a particular category of geographical feature.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are described as how or why a feature is."
Relationships are described as how or why a feature is.
fib: ______ means of representing landforms or relief features on maps is by the use of contour lines.
commonest
The commonest means of representing landforms or relief features on maps is by the use of contour lines.
______ are used to map two-dimensional or polygonal features; that is, features that significantly cover a wide area of land.
Area (or areal) symbols
Area symbols
Area (or areal) symbols are used to map two-dimensional or polygonal features; that is, features that significantly cover a wide area of land.
______ are used to map point or zero-dimensional features.
Point symbols
Point symbols are used to map point or zero-dimensional features.
______ is a narrow long chain or range of highlands (Fig. 5.6).
ridge
Ridge A ridge is a narrow long chain or range of highlands (Fig. 5.6).
______ is an isolated one family residence.
homestead
Homestead A homestead is an isolated one family residence.
______ are used to code or set data and present it in form of a diagram or illustration.
symbols
The symbols are used to code or set data and present it in form of a diagram or illustration.
______ is the prime meridian, which represents 0º longitude.
starting point
The starting point is the prime meridian, which represents 0º longitude.
______ is a method by which the curved surface of the earth is represented on a flat surface.
projection
A projection is a method by which the curved surface of the earth is represented on a flat surface.
______ are called eastings, since they increase in value as you travel east on the map.
vertical lines
The vertical lines are called eastings, since they increase in value as you travel east on the map.
______ is the linear distance round the edge or boundary of an aerial feature.
Perimeter
Perimeter is the linear distance round the edge or boundary of an aerial feature.
______ are used to encode and communicate geographical information.
Map symbols
Map symbols are used to encode and communicate geographical information.
______ are called northings, since they increase in value as you travel north on the map.
horizontal lines
The horizontal lines are called northings, since they increase in value as you travel north on the map.
______ are used to represent one-dimensional or linear features such as roads, rivers, railways, pipelines, and power or telecommunication cables.
Line symbols
Line symbols are used to represent one-dimensional or linear features such as roads, rivers, railways, pipelines, and power or telecommunication cables.
______ is a way of representing on a two-dimensional surface, (a paper, a computer monitor, etc.) any real- world location or object.
map
A map is a way of representing on a two-dimensional surface, (a paper, a computer monitor, etc.) any real- world location or object.
______ is any recognisable individual feature that exists at a spot or single location.
point feature
A point feature is any recognisable individual feature that exists at a spot or single location.
